headline: Thanksgiving's strong storm is moving past, with the Wind Advisory around Charlotte and the region ending by 10 AM and rain tapering off, but gusty southwest winds return this afternoon into a cold Friday before a milder weekend and a cold front bringing rain, now trending heavier, late Sunday into early Monday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A strong low pressure system moves onshore along the Carolina coast this Thanksgiving morning and lifts north tonight. Strong gusts early this morning can still knock down tents and holiday decorations and cause isolated power outages, but winds should ease substantially as the storm passes to the east, and the Wind Advisory expires at 10 AM (it may be canceled early). Rain tapers off later this morning, possibly lingering to mid-morning around Charlotte and east of the mountains, and little more heavy rain is expected, though leaf-clogged storm drains could cause some localized poor-drainage flooding. Winds turn southwest and become gusty again this afternoon and tonight, gusting 25 to 35 mph, below advisory level, while low clouds hang on into early evening and rain wrapping around the storm turns to snow showers along the North Carolina–Tennessee border this evening.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Snow showers near the Tennessee border tonight into Friday should leave less than an inch at most spots, with isolated 1 to 3 inches possible, while areas east of the mountain crest stay dry. Friday is cool, with highs about 10 degrees below normal, frequent southwest gusts of 25 to 35 mph easing Friday evening, and a gray low-cloud deck possibly lingering. Saturday is dry and quiet as high pressure returns and temperatures warm back to near normal.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Another strong storm tracks northeast across the Midwest and lower Great Lakes Sunday into Monday morning, pushing a cold front through the area Sunday afternoon into early Monday. Rain chances and amounts have trended higher with more moisture ahead of the front, but excessive rainfall looks unlikely. Dry high pressure follows, with temperatures near normal from Monday onward.

watch_for: Strong gusts until about 10 AM Thursday that can topple tents and decorations or cause isolated outages
Southwest gusts of 25–35 mph Thursday afternoon through Friday; an advisory isn't planned unless forecasts trend stronger
Rain from Sunday's cold front, trending heavier late Sunday into early Monday
confidence: Forecasters say Thanksgiving's forecast is mostly unchanged and the snow near the Tennessee border should be minimal, while rain amounts for the Sunday night front are still trending upward.
